description:
Port 2 reference extensions to prove the system works end-to-end.

**1. dirty-repo-guard** (cancel-on-result pattern)
- Subscribes to: session_before_switch
- Checks if git working tree is dirty (uncommitted changes)
- If dirty: returns {:cancel, "uncommitted changes in repo"}
- Prevents session switch when there's unsaved work
- Tests: guard blocks on dirty, allows on clean, handles non-git dirs

**2. input-transform** (reduce-chain pattern)
- Subscribes to: input
- Example: expands shorthand like "fix" → "fix the failing test"
- Or: strips dangerous patterns from user input
- Returns {:transform, new_text, images} or :continue
- Tests: transforms matching input, passes through non-matching

These prove:
- Extension discovery and loading works
- Handler registration via api.on() works
- cancel-on-result dispatch works (dirty-repo-guard)
- reduce-chain dispatch works (input-transform)
- Telemetry fires for both success and error cases
- Error in one extension doesn't crash others

**Definition of done from epic:** "a custom extension can register a
tool_call handler that sanitizes bash commands and a session_before_switch
handler that blocks on a dirty repo"

**Upstream ref:** Various built-in extensions in coding-agent
title: Reference extensions: dirty-repo-guard + input-transform
